s1.syndrome_frame: Ocular inflammation with eyelid involvement and conjunctival hyperemia in a patient with a history of autoimmune disease
salient_findings: Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
key_facts: Switched to adalimumab due to disease relapse
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
Rest of the ophthalmic examination was unremarkable

shortlist.label: Blepharitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous eyelids with crusty plaques on the eyelid margins

shortlist.label: Crohn disease-associated ocular inflammation
shortlist.why_kept: History of biopsy-proven Crohn disease and ocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Infliximab-induced ocular inflammation
shortlist.why_kept: Initial treatment with infliximab and subsequent ocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Adalimumab-induced ocular inflammation
shortlist.why_kept: Switch to adalimumab due to disease relapse and ongoing ocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Eczematous blepharoconjunctivitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral eyelid involvement with ectropion and diffuse conjunctival hyperemia

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous eyelids, ectropion, and crusty plaques on the eyelid margins are consistent with blepharitis.

rejected.label: Crohn disease-associated ocular inflammation
rejected.why: While the patient has Crohn disease, the specific ocular symptoms described are more consistent with blepharitis than a direct manifestation of Crohn disease.

rejected.label: Infliximab-induced ocular inflammation
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms persisted after switching from infliximab to adalimumab, suggesting that the ocular inflammation is not solely due to infliximab.

rejected.label: Adalimumab-induced ocular inflammation
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms were present before switching to adalimumab, and there is no clear indication that adalimumab is the primary cause of the ocular inflammation.

rejected.label: Eczematous blepharoconjunctivitis
rejected.why: While this condition could explain some of the patient's symptoms, the specific description of crusty plaques on the eyelid margins and diffuse conjunctival hyperemia is more consistent with blepharitis.
